issues.body: The routing changes explicitly retain `opus5` as a continuity fallback for implementation, and `auto-mint-provenance.py` now correctly refuses to guess whether Sol or Opus authored a PR. But this file simultaneously changes the manual writer's sole accepted provider to `openai`: `ORCHESTRATOR_IMPL_PROVIDER = "openai"`, so `alias_mint_refusal("opus5", ...)` refuses. Therefore a PR genuinely implemented by the permitted Opus fallback cannot be auto-minted and cannot be manually attested truthfully either. It remains without a record and invisible to the provenance-derived cross-provider lane, contradicting the claimed continuity fallback and the comments that describe the manual workflow as the recovery path. The tests only prove that Anthropic aliases are rejected; they do not demonstrate any end-to-end admission path for the fallback the live route permits.
issues.fix_hint: Provide a sound recovery path that accepts trustworthy per-PR implementation evidence and records either provider, then selects the opposite review provider, while retaining SHA binding and fail-closed validation. Add an end-to-end test for an Opus-fallback-authored PR proving that it can be truthfully recorded as Anthropic and routed to OpenAI review. If the provenance design intentionally supports only Sol-authored PRs, remove Opus from the implementation routes instead of advertising an unusable fallback.
issues.title: The permitted Opus fallback has no truthful provenance recovery path

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The prior round's false-attestation blocker is fixed: the unattended sweep now refuses rather than inventing Sol provenance. However, the change leaves the explicitly supported Opus implementation fallback with no provenance path at all. Auto-mint refuses it because evidence is absent, while the only advertised recovery writer now rejects the truthful Anthropic alias. Such PRs cannot enter the cross-provider review lane, so the new fallback policy is incomplete and does not deliver continuity. This is a new major finding, so progress is regressing under the required scale.
